heading: INT. CONSERVATORY GREENHOUSE - ORCHID SHOW - DAY

units.text: INT. CONSERVATORY GREENHOUSE - ORCHID SHOW - DAY
Glass and humid green.
Ten thousand blossoms on risers: slipper orchids like lacquered tongues, moth orchids like frozen flight.
Rain ticks on the panes overhead.
WREN ASHBY-LOVELACE, 30s, in a cardigan the color of moss, bends close to a speckled bloom with a magnifying glass, entirely absorbed.
A STRANGER, 30s, a woman in a rain-darkened trench and a scarf the red of a struck match, stops beside her.
She does not look at the orchids.
She looks at Wren.
That one is lying to you.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Excuse me?
units.name: WREN

units.text: The label says Paphiopedilum. But it's a hybrid. Look at the staminode.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Wren lowers the glass.
Looks.
Looks again.
She laughs, low and surprised.
You're right. She's right. Whoever grew it, I mean.
units.name: WREN

units.text: She'd be furious with you for guessing.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: MR. ABARA, 60s, a show steward with a lapel rosette, glides by with a clipboard and clears his throat.
Ladies, the judging begins at noon. Kindly keep to the path.
units.name: MR. ABARA

units.text: He moves on.
The two women watch him go, then glance at each other, conspirators.
I'm Wren.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Tamsin.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She extends her hand.
Wren takes it.
Neither lets go at once.
Above, the rain thickens.
TAMSIN lifts her scarf, and, shyly, shows Wren the orchid pinned beneath it: a hybrid, speckled, impossible.
I grew it for the judging. I was going to lose on purpose.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Don't. Not today.
units.name: WREN
